title_jp: {留学|りゅうがく}、どう{思う|おもう}？
context: Friday 4 December, after school at {鷹ノ原高校|たかのはらこうこう}: {佐藤|さとう}{先生|せんせい} has asked アルちゃん in to help {澪|みお} prepare for the interview for the school's summer exchange to Canada. {澪|みお} asks his opinion and is sure her parents will say no.
scene: Friday after school in the English room. {佐藤|さとう}{先生|せんせい} asked you in: {澪|みお} wants to study abroad and needs your opinion.

phrases.jp: どう{思う|おもう}？{正直|しょうじき|honestly|4}に{言って|いって}。
phrases.en: What do you think? Tell me honestly.
phrases.note: Asking a friend for a real opinion, not a polite one.

phrases.jp: あんなに{頑張った|がんばった}んだから、{合格|ごうかく|passing (an exam)|3}するに{違いない|ちがいない}。
phrases.en: After working that hard, they're bound to pass.
phrases.note: Reason + んだから + strong conclusion.

phrases.jp: {賛成|さんせい|agreeing, in favour|3}だけど、ちょっと{心配|しんぱい}もある。
phrases.en: I'm for it, but I'm a bit worried too.
phrases.note: A soft opinion: agree, then add a 'but'.

phrases.jp: {人|ひと}によって{意見|いけん}が{違う|ちがう}よね。
phrases.en: Opinions differ from person to person, don't they?
phrases.note: A safe way to avoid taking sides.

phrases.jp: {自分|じぶん}の{将来|しょうらい|future|4}は、{自分|じぶん}で{決めたい|きめたい}。
phrases.en: I want to decide my own future myself.
phrases.note: A strong personal opinion, said calmly.

dialogue_setting: The English room at {鷹ノ原高校|たかのはらこうこう}, Friday after school. Snow outside; the brass band is practising somewhere down the corridor.

dialogue.speaker: 佐藤先生
dialogue.jp: アルちゃん、{今日|きょう}はありがとうございます。{澪|みお}さんが{留学|りゅうがく|studying abroad|3}の{面接|めんせつ|interview|3}を{受ける|うける}そうです。
dialogue.en: アルちゃん, thank you for coming today. {澪|みお}さん is going to do the interview for studying abroad.

dialogue.speaker: 澪
dialogue.jp: アルちゃん、{正直|しょうじき|honestly|4}どう{思う|おもう}？{若い|わかい}うちに{留学|りゅうがく|studying abroad|3}したほうがいい？
dialogue.en: アルちゃん, honestly, what do you think? Is it better to study abroad while you're young?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {僕|ぼく}は{賛成|さんせい|agreeing, in favour|3}。{世界|せかい}が{広がる|ひろがる|to widen, spread|3}と{思う|おもう}よ。
dialogue.en: I'm all for it. I think your world gets bigger.

dialogue.speaker: 澪
dialogue.jp: でもうちの{親|おや|parent(s)|4}、{絶対|ぜったい}{反対|はんたい}するに{違いない|ちがいない}っしょ。お{金|かね}も{かかる||to cost (money, time)|4}し。
dialogue.en: But my parents are definitely going to say no, for sure. And it costs money.
dialogue.note: Teen slang: っしょ = でしょう.

dialogue.speaker: 佐藤先生
dialogue.jp: {奨学金|しょうがくきん|scholarship|3}もありますよ。{本気|ほんき}だと{伝えれば|つたえれば}、ご{両親|りょうしん|parents|4}も{分かって|わかって}くださるに{違いありません|ちがいありません}。
dialogue.en: There are scholarships too. If you tell them you're serious, I'm sure your parents will understand.

dialogue.speaker: 澪
dialogue.jp: …じゃあ{今夜|こんや}、{親|おや|parent(s)|4}に{相談|そうだん|talking over, asking advice|4}してみる。{練習|れんしゅう}、ガチで{付き合って|つきあって}ね！
dialogue.en: …OK, I'll talk to my parents tonight. And you're properly helping me practise, OK?
dialogue.note: Slang: ガチで = {本気|ほんき}で. {付|つ}き{合|あ}う here = keep someone company, help.

listening.intro: {佐藤|さとう}{先生|せんせい} tells you when the interview is. Type what she says.

lines.jp: {面接|めんせつ|interview|3}は{来週|らいしゅう}の{金曜日|きんようび}、{放課後|ほうかご|after school|3}です。
lines.en: The interview is next Friday, after school.

grammar.form: verb / い-adj plain + に{違|ちが}いない ({反対|はんたい}するに{違|ちが}いない, {高|たか}いに{違|ちが}いない) · noun / な-adj: no だ + に{違|ちが}いない ({本当|ほんとう}に{違|ちが}いない, {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}に{違|ちが}いない) · polite: に{違|ちが}いありません
grammar.explanation: A guess the speaker feels sure about: 'must be, I bet'. Stronger than だろう, and a bit written or dramatic, so in chat people often just say {絶対|ぜったい}… or きっと…. Nouns and な-adjectives drop だ: {本当|ほんとう}に{違|ちが}いない, not {本当|ほんとう}だに{違|ちが}いない.
mark: 分かってくださるに違いありません
起きているに違いない

examples.jp: こんなに{並んで|ならんで|to line up|4}る。{有名|ゆうめい}な{店|みせ}に{違いない|ちがいない}。
examples.en: Look at this queue. It must be a famous place.

examples.jp: {電気|でんき}がついてる。{健太|けんた}はまだ{起きて|おきて}いるに{違いない|ちがいない}。
examples.en: The light's on. {健太|けんた} must still be up.

quiz.question: あんなに{練習|れんしゅう}したんだから、{合格|ごうかく|passing (an exam)|3}＿＿。
quiz.en: After practising that much, she's bound to pass.
quiz.explain: Plain verb + に{違|ちが}いない; the particle is always に.

quiz_more.question: この{財布|さいふ|wallet|4}、{健太|けんた}の＿＿。いつもここに{置く|おく}から。
quiz_more.en: This wallet must be {健太|けんた}'s. He always leaves it here.
quiz_more.explain: Nouns drop だ: {健太|けんた}のに{違|ちが}いない.

quiz_more.question: {間違いない|まちがいない}！{犯人|はんにん|culprit|2}はあの{人|ひと}＿＿！
quiz_more.en: No doubt about it! The culprit must be that person!
quiz_more.explain: Total certainty → に{違|ちが}いない. かもしれない is only 'maybe'.

kanji.where: The sign on the door next to the English room, with university brochures piled outside.
kanji.breakdown: {進路|しんろ}{指導|しどう}{室|しつ}: 進路 path forward + 指導 guidance + 室 room → the room where teachers help you choose your path.
kanji.related: {進路|しんろ} alone = your plans after school: {進路|しんろ}はどうするの？

tip.title: The three-way meeting
tip.body: In Japanese high schools, big decisions go through a {三者面談|さんしゃめんだん}: student, parent and teacher sit down together. Students rarely decide alone, so 'I'll talk to my parents' ({親|おや}に{相談|そうだん}する) is the normal first step, not a sign of being childish.

challenge.prompt: {佐藤|さとう}{先生|せんせい}: 「{澪|みお}さんの{面接|めんせつ|interview|3}、どう{思いますか|おもいますか}。」 You answer that you're sure she'll be fine. One part is wrong.

parts.why: な-adjectives drop だ before に{違|ちが}いない: {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}に.

challenge.model_answer: {澪|みお}さんなら、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}に{違いない|ちがいない}と{思います|おもいます}。
challenge.explanation: 〜なら sets up {澪|みお}さん as the person you're judging. {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ} is a な-adjective, so it joins に{違|ちが}いない directly, with no だ. と{思|おも}います softens the strong guess and keeps it polite for a teacher.
challenge.hint: な-adj + に{違|ちが}いない (no だ)

vocab.note: {留学|りゅうがく}する. A student from abroad: {留学生|りゅうがくせい}.
{面|めん} face + {接|せつ} meet. For jobs and schools; {面接|めんせつ}を{受|う}ける.
Opposite of {反対|はんたい}. 〜に{賛成|さんせい}する = agree with.
{世界|せかい}が{広|ひろ}がる = your world opens up. Also news or fire spreading.
Your own parents, casually. うちの{親|おや} = my folks.
お{金|かね}がかかる, {時間|じかん}がかかる. Usually in kana.
In Japan many are loans you pay back; a grant is {給付型|きゅうふがた}.
{両|りょう} both + {親|しん} parent. Someone else's: ご{両親|りょうしん}.
〜に{相談|そうだん}する = ask someone's advice. ちょっと{相談|そうだん}が… = can I ask you something?

kanji_study.parts: 卯 a gate pinned shut on top + 田 field → something held in place over the field: stay, keep.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 貿 (trade): 貿 has 貝 shell (money) underneath, 留 has 田 field.

kanji_study.parts: 木 tree + 目 eye → looking closely at a tree, face to face with it: each other, mutual.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 想 (idea): 想 is 相 with 心 heart underneath.

extras.title: Giving an opinion
extras.intro: Ways to say what you think, from soft to firm.

items.jp: どちらかと{言えば|いえば}、{賛成|さんせい|in favour|3}です。
items.note: A soft, very Japanese way to lean one way.

items.jp: {私|わたし}としては、{反対|はんたい}です。
items.note: としては = speaking for myself.

items.jp: {人|ひと}それぞれだと{思う|おもう}。
items.en: I think it's up to each person.

extras.title_jp: {若者|わかもの|young people|3}{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: What {澪|みお} and her friends say. Slang: use only with friends.

items.note: = {本気|ほんき}・{本当|ほんとう}. ガチで{楽しい|たのしい}.
Polite way to say 'not good'. Very common.
